ok can u edit my text to my mom pls. its sunday so i have to send before she gets busy at the salon

her last msg: "Dinner is at 8 tonight, I leave a plate for you since you close. Did you pick your pharmacy classes for spring yet?"

Here's a polished version that keeps your casual tone:

"Ok Ma, thank you for the plate! I can help at the front desk from 2 to 5 today after my cafe shift. Also, I'm thinking of taking Intro to Nutrition in spring. It looks interesting and I've really liked the digestion unit. Priority registration opens Nov 18 at 7 a.m., so I'd like to decide soon."

I trimmed the "has nothing to do with anything" line, since it sounds like you're apologizing for the class. Want it shorter or softer?

can u make it sound more like an idea than a decision.. like i dont want to get into it about pharmacy rn

and i skipped her pharmacy question on purpose lol

Sure. This version frames it as something you're mulling over and doesn't answer the pharmacy question directly:

"Ok Ma, thank you for the plate! I can help at the front desk from 2 to 5 today after my cafe shift. Also, I've been thinking it might be fun to add Intro to Nutrition in spring, just an idea for now. Registration opens Nov 18 at 7 a.m., so I'm looking at options this week. Can we talk about classes after dinner?"

The last line moves the class talk to later, so it doesn't turn into a debate over text. Cut it if you'd rather not set up a conversation.

On the form, the layout looks clean. Here's what I checked:
- Your ID is entered in a single field with no stray characters. Compare it against your student card to be sure it matches.
- Name, term and fee are each on their own line and consistent.
- The payment line says fee waiver request, but a fee amount is listed above it. Check whether the form wants $0 or the full amount when you request a waiver.

One other thing: Fall 2026 is an unusual term to list for a spring transfer. Confirm the term you want before you submit.
